introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0760), Paper 2 - Cameroon History Since 1800, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Candidates are required to answer FOUR questions, choosing at least ONE from each of the sections. All the questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Regle de choix : le sujet impose « answer FOUR questions, choosing at least ONE from each of the sections » (3 sections : A 1800-1922, B 1922-1961, C 1961 to present, 4 questions chacune, numerotation continue 1 a 12). `regles_choix` porte le minimum impose, une regle `parmi 1 sur 4` par section ; la regle « 4 questions en tout » n'est pas exprimable et est recopiee dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : chaque question est imprimee « (25 marks) » et la page de garde dit « All the questions carry equal marks » ; `points` de l'exercice et de la question unique valent 25. Aucun ecart avec le sujet (4 x 25 = 100).

Defauts d'impression du sujet : scan de deux pages (CamScanner) avec filigrane gcerevision.com et bandeau publicitaire, sans incidence sur la lecture, mais avec une legere transparence de texte (verso) en haut de la page 2 et entre quelques questions ; les intitules de section sont imprimes avec un tiret demi-cadratin (« 1800 - 1922 ») recopie avec un tiret simple ; la question 2 est imprimee « succeed to extend » (tournure incorrecte, recopiee telle quelle) ; la question 3 est ambigue (« the results of German annexation by 1884 ») ; la question 6 est maladroite (« indigenous resistance and failure against French rule »). Aucune figure, carte ni document dans le sujet. Page de garde verifiee : ADVANCED LEVEL, History 2, Paper 2 - Cameroon History Since 1800, code 0760, JUNE 2026 (reference GCE26/0760/2/BN).

Aucun corrige officiel : les corriges sont des reponses modeles redigees de memoire, sans acces a une source. Les dates, noms et traites sont ceux de l'historiographie etablie ; les faits dont la precision est moindre sont formules prudemment ou sans chiffre. Aucune citation, statistique ni source n'est inventee. Les corriges sont a relire par un historien du Cameroun avant diffusion.

Question 10 : question dont les donnees precises sont les plus difficiles a verifier de memoire. Le corrige reste general : place de la CDC et des cooperatives de cafe et de cacao, du West Cameroon Marketing Board, des routes, de l'education et de la sante, des plans quinquennaux federaux, du remplacement de la monnaie (livre -> franc CFA au debut des annees 1960). Aucun chiffre (production, budget, effectifs, kilometres) n'est donne ; les noms d'organismes ne sont cites que s'ils sont tres connus. A faire relire par un historien du Cameroun avant diffusion.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Assess the socio-economic development of West Cameroon between 1961 and 1972.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** From 1 October 1961 to 1972 West Cameroon (the former British Southern Cameroons) was a federated state of the Federal Republic of Cameroon, with its own Prime Minister (Foncha, then A.N. Jua from 1965 and S.T. Muna from 1968) and House of Assembly. "Assess" means to weigh achievements against limits. West Cameroon was a mainly agricultural, rural territory with few towns and little industry, and its development was shaped by the federal framework as well as by its own resources.

**1. Economic development: achievements.**
(a) *Agriculture and cash crops.* The economy rested on agriculture. The plantations around Mount Cameroon, run largely by the Cameroons Development Corporation (CDC) and private companies, produced bananas, rubber, palm products and tea, and were the biggest employers. Smallholders produced cocoa (Kumba and Mamfe areas), coffee (the Grassfields, including Arabica coffee) and palm produce. The cooperative movement and the West Cameroon Marketing Board helped farmers to market their crops.
(b) *Transport and communications.* Roads linking Buea, Kumba, Mamfe, Bamenda and Wum were improved and extended, with some federal and foreign aid, and the ports of Tiko and Victoria (Limbe) and the airfields were used to export crops.
(c) *Development institutions.* The West Cameroon government and federal plans promoted agricultural and rural projects and a number of development agencies and services, and the first federal development plans (from 1961) included West Cameroon.
(d) *Public finance and services.* The West Cameroon administration kept a functioning civil service, an inherited system of local government and (for some years) a sound budget. Water supply and electricity were extended in the main towns.

**2. Social development.**
(a) *Education.* Primary education expanded, mostly through the missions and government with grants, and secondary schools and teacher training colleges increased; some bilingual schools were opened. West Cameroonians could also attend the new Federal University of Yaoundé (founded in 1962).
(b) *Health.* Hospitals and health centres (government and mission) were extended, and campaigns against endemic diseases continued.
(c) *Urbanisation and employment.* Towns such as Victoria, Kumba, Buea, Tiko and Bamenda grew, and wage employment in the plantations, the civil service and trade expanded.

**3. Limits and problems.**
(a) *Dependence on a few exports.* The economy remained agricultural and dependent on bananas, coffee and cocoa, whose prices could fall and whose markets were exposed to competition; there was almost no industry or processing, and industrial investment went mainly to the East (Douala).
(b) *Federal centralisation.* From the early 1960s economic and financial decisions were increasingly taken in Yaoundé: the currency was unified (the CFA franc replaced the pound in the early 1960s), and planning, banking, customs and taxes came under federal control, which reduced the state's financial autonomy and left West Cameroon dependent on federal funds.
(c) *Poor infrastructure.* Roads outside the main axes were often impassable in the rainy season, the Grassfields remained poorly connected to the ports and the rest of the country, and electricity and water supply were limited.
(d) *Limited health and educational capacity.* The provision of secondary and higher education and of qualified staff remained small compared to need.
(e) *Political changes.* The creation of a single party, the Cameroon National Union (1966), and the end of competitive politics reduced the ability of West Cameroon's leaders to defend its interests, and the sense of neglect and unequal treatment grew.

**4. Assessment.** West Cameroon made progress in these years: output of cash crops, roads, schools and health care all expanded, and it kept a reputation for orderly administration. But the progress was modest, was based on a narrow agricultural economy and was restricted by the centralising tendencies of the federal government. Compared with East Cameroon, it received little industrial investment.

**Conclusion.** The socio-economic development of West Cameroon between 1961 and 1972 was real but limited: agriculture, transport, education and health improved, but there was little industry and growing federal control, so that the state remained a mainly rural and dependent part of the Federation.
